title: Egyptian Pairs
statement: How many ordered pairs of positive integers $(a, b)$ satisfy $\dfrac1a + \dfrac1b = \dfrac1{12}$?
hints: Clear denominators and try to factor. Simon's favourite factoring trick helps.
solution: The equation becomes $ab - 12a - 12b = 0$, that is $(a-12)(b-12) = 144$. Both factors must be positive, since $a < 12$ would make $\frac1a > \frac1{12}$. So the pairs match the divisors of $144 = 2^4 3^2$, and there are $5\cdot 3 = 15$.
